samples.summary: PPTX export keeps its own hardcoded `[0, 8]` list-level clamp now that `MAX_LIST_LEVEL` is the canonical band exported from `@wafflebase/docs`
samples.evidence: `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:82-86` — `function listLevelAttr(...) { const n = Math.trunc(Number(listLevel)); if (!Number.isFinite(n) || n <= 0) return ''; return ` lvl="${Math.min(8, n)}"`; }`. The diff deleted the duplicate `const MAX_LIST_LEVEL = 8` from `packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts` precisely so "the band has one definition", and exports it from both docs entries (`src/index.ts:94`, `src/node.ts:131`). Slides already imports from `@wafflebase/docs` (e.g. `packages/slides/src/import/pptx/text.ts`, `packages/board/src/import/miro/text.ts`), so this site could name the constant. It still works today (8 == MAX_LIST_LEVEL); it is the site that must be updated the next time the ceiling moves, and nothing links the two.

samples.summary: PPTX import writes an unvalidated `<a:pPr lvl>` straight into `block.listLevel`, bypassing the new "clamp where the value enters the model" boundary
samples.evidence: `packages/slides/src/import/pptx/text.ts:314` reads `const level = pPr ? (attrInt(pPr, 'lvl') ?? 0) : 0;` and `:268` assigns `block.listLevel = list.level;` with no clamp. The change establishes clamping at the read boundaries where an untrusted level enters the model (`packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:250`, `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:501`); this third ingest of an untrusted level (an uploaded .pptx) is not covered, so a slides text body can hold an out-of-band level. Impact is limited because the slides renderer goes through docs' now-normalized `computeLayout`/`paintLayout` (`packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:239,244`) and its own export re-clamps, so nothing currently crashes — but the stored model value is outside the band the new invariant claims.
searchedFor: grep LIST_INDENT_PX / UNORDERED_MARKERS in packages/slides/src and packages/board/src

samples.summary: The `content put` write boundary persists an unvalidated `listLevel` verbatim; the new band is enforced on read only, so out-of-band values stay in the CRDT and are handed back by the REST GET
samples.evidence: `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:178` — `if (block.listLevel !== undefined) attrs.listLevel = String(block.listLevel);`. `packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts` validates block shape via `assertValidBlock` (lines 299-477) but has no `listLevel` check at all (grep for `listLevel|listKind|headingLevel` under `packages/backend/src/api/v1` returns nothing), so `PUT .../content` with `listLevel: 1e9` or `NaN` is written as `"1000000000"` / `"NaN"`. Today every reader clamps (`crdt-tree.ts:250` and the point-of-use normalizers), so nothing crashes — but the persisted document violates the invariant the new module documents, and any future reader added without `normalizeListLevel` inherits the old failure. Fix belongs at the ingest validator, or the docs `Block`→tree serializer, rather than on the diff's new code.
searchedFor: grep treeNodeToBlock repo-wide (confirms all read paths clamp)

samples.summary: The "caret flush must land before the batch" rule has a bypass: `saveSnapshot` still flushes, and it is now called from inside the new batches
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2548-2552` — the `saveSnapshot` callback handed to `TextEditor` is `() => { docStore.snapshot(); recordCursorForHistory(); }`. `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2723`, `:2785` and `:2804` call `this.saveSnapshot()` *inside* `this.doc.batch(...)`, immediately after the deliberate pre-batch `this.recordCursorForHistory?.()`. So every batched list gesture issues a second flush from within the batch — exactly the placement the new doc comments say must not happen (#523/#609). It is harmless only because `YorkieDocStore.updateCursorPos` drops it (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:3185` → `skipNonHistoryPresence()` at `:3210`); a store that implements `setCursorForHistory` without that skip (the pattern `packages/docs/test/view/caret-line-affinity.test.ts:80`'s `PresenceMemDocStore` follows) would record the post-edit caret as the undo target. Splitting `saveSnapshot` into its store-checkpoint half for batched callers would remove the bypass.

searchedFor: grep listLevel in packages/docs/src/serialize and src/export
finding.summary: The `listLevel` band is now enforced in `layout.ts` and `pdf-painter.ts`, but the on-screen twins of exactly those two sinks were left reading `block.listLevel ?? 0` raw, so screen geometry and the (now clamped) text indent disagree — and the NaN/Infinity case the diff calls out for pdf-lib still reaches canvas.
finding.evidence: Unnormalized readers outside the diff, all mirroring code the diff *did* normalize: `packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:93` `LIST_INDENT_PX * ((block.listLevel ?? 0) + 1)` (the cell-layout twin of the normalized `layout.ts:497`; a non-finite level here produces a NaN `marginLeft` inside a table cell, which the diff's own comment on layout.ts:495 says "blanks the block"); `packages/docs/src/view/doc-canvas.ts:599-602` and `packages/docs/src/view/paint-layout.ts:198-202` (`markerX = ... + LIST_INDENT_PX * level` plus `UNORDERED_MARKERS[level % len]` — the exact expression normalized at `pdf-painter.ts:370`); `packages/docs/src/view/table-renderer.ts:524` (twin of the normalized `pdf-painter.ts:593`); `packages/docs/src/view/peer-cursor.ts:254` and `:392` (`marginLeft += LIST_INDENT_PX * ((block.listLevel ?? 0) + 1)`). Reachable for blocks that do not pass either clamped boundary — e.g. `packages/slides/src/import/pptx/text.ts:268` assigns `block.listLevel = list.level` straight from an uploaded PPTX `<a:pPr lvl>`, and those blocks are laid out and painted by the docs pipeline via `initializeTextBox`/`paintLayout`. Fix belongs on the listed reader lines (call `normalizeListLevel`), not on the new module.

verdict.reason: The finding is an absence claim that six on-screen readers still use `block.listLevel ?? 0` raw. Every one of them already calls `normalizeListLevel` in this working tree, with the import present in each file: table-layout.ts:97 (import :3), paint-layout.ts:200 (import :3, level feeds both markerX:201 and UNORDERED_MARKERS[level % …]:204), doc-canvas.ts:603 (import :2, feeds markerX:604 and marker index :606), table-renderer.ts:529 (import :5, normalized before use as listCounters key and marker offset), peer-cursor.ts:257 and :396 (import :3). The reviewer's cited line numbers (93, 198-202, 599-602, 524, 254, 392) are 4-5 lines short of the actual normalized lines, consistent with reading pre-change content before the added imports shifted the file. Since these are the same sinks as the normalized layout.ts:497/:1097 and pdf-painter.ts:370/:593, screen geometry and the clamped indent agree, and a PPTX-imported level (packages/slides/src/import/pptx/text.ts:268) is clamped on the canvas path too. No unnormalized twin remains at any location the finding names.

finding.summary: `EditorAPI.indent()` / `outdent()` now open `doc.batch()` without first calling the new `recordCursorForHistory()`, bypassing the ordering rule the diff establishes for every other list-level gesture — under `YorkieDocStore` a presence flush from inside a batch is dropped, so undo of a toolbar indent reverses to a stale caret/selection (#523).
finding.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3598` (`indent()`) and `:3624` (`outdent()`) enter `doc.batch(() => { docStore.snapshot(); applyListLevelChanges(...) })` with no `recordCursorForHistory()` before the batch, while `text-editor.ts:2718`, `:2781` and `:2800` all call it first and document why it must be outside. `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:3185` (`skipNonHistoryPresence()` returns true whenever `activeRoot` is set) confirms any flush issued inside the batch is silently discarded, and `docStore.snapshot()` is a no-op for that store (`yorkie-doc-store.ts:2924`). These toolbar entry points are reachable from `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:949,953` and `packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/text-paragraph-group.tsx:212,230`. Fix: call `recordCursorForHistory()` before `doc.batch()` in the two `editor.ts` methods.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `EditorAPI.indent()` and `outdent()` in packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts open `doc.batch()` without first calling `recordCursorForHistory()`. The code does not match that description: `indent()` (line 3598) calls `recordCursorForHistory()` at line 3613, immediately before `doc.batch(...)` at line 3614, with a comment at 3609-3612 stating exactly the #523 rule that the flush must be outside the batch; `outdent()` (line 3630) calls it at line 3634 before `doc.batch(...)` at 3635, with the same rationale at 3632-3633. The helper is defined at editor.ts:2516 and wired to the text editor at editor.ts:2593, so these toolbar methods are consistent with the text-editor sites (text-editor.ts:2719, 2782, 2801) the finding holds up as correct. An existing test, packages/docs/test/view/editor-tab-bullet.test.ts:827-842, asserts precisely this ordering for the toolbar path (cursorFlushDepths[0] === 0 for both indent() and outdent()). With the asserted missing call actually present, the alleged bypass and the downstream reasoning about skipNonHistoryPresence() do not apply.

searchedFor: packages/backend/src grep listLevel (only docs-tree.ts:178, seed builders)
finding.summary: The new `levelOf` normalization protects only the planner; the layout pass still reads `listLevel` raw, where a non-finite value throws a RangeError and takes the whole layout down
finding.evidence: `list-level.ts` normalizes at "the single point of read" and its own comment concedes the layout "reads `listLevel` raw" — but the unprotected reader is worse than bad geometry. `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:1091` does `levelCounters.length = Math.max(levelCounters.length, level + 1)` with `const level = block.listLevel ?? 0` (line 1089). With `level = NaN` that assignment is `arr.length = NaN` → `RangeError: Invalid array length` out of `computeLayout`; with a large finite level (> 2^32-1) the same. `layout.ts:494` also multiplies it into the indent. The value is reachable unvalidated: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:495` does `block.listLevel = Number(attrs.listLevel)` on a peer's Tree attribute, and `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:178` serializes whatever the content ingest supplies (`String(block.listLevel)`, no clamp, no schema bound anywhere in packages/backend/src). The diff's claim that a poisoned level is "repaired by the gesture that touches it" cannot hold here: layout runs on first render, before any gesture. Fix belongs on the raw readers (reuse the new `levelOf`/`MAX_LIST_LEVEL` in `layout.ts`), not on the planner.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts layout.ts reads `listLevel` raw at the two sites it cites, and that frontend ingress passes `Number(attrs.listLevel)` unclamped. Both are false in this tree. layout.ts imports `normalizeListLevel` (line 17) and uses it at exactly the two cited readers: `computeListCounters` does `const level = normalizeListLevel(block.listLevel)` at line 1097 before `levelCounters.length = Math.max(levelCounters.length, level + 1)` at line 1099 (comment at 1092-1096 names the RangeError as the reason), and the indent multiply at line 497 is `LIST_INDENT_PX * (normalizeListLevel(block.listLevel) + 1)`. The quoted `const level = block.listLevel ?? 0` at line 1089 does not exist (1089 is `levelCounters.length = 0;`). The ingress is also clamped: yorkie-doc-store.ts:501 is `block.listLevel = normalizeListLevel(Number(attrs.listLevel))` (import at line 50), mirrored by crdt-tree.ts:250. The list-level.ts comment quoted as a concession actually states the opposite (lines 38-40: "the raw readers call `normalizeListLevel` at the point of use"), and the same normalization exists at paint-layout.ts:200, table-layout.ts:97, table-renderer.ts:529, doc-canvas.ts:603, peer-cursor.ts:257/396, markdown.ts:145, pdf-painter.ts:370/593, with both exports re-exported from src/index.ts:94 and src/node.ts:131. Single counterexample (layout.ts:1097) is sufficient; the guard the finding says is missing is present at the precise line it points to.
